---
title: Displays and local dashboard
---

## Notebook and terminal

`progress=True` selects an anywidget notebook display when available, otherwise a Rich terminal display. Both show sampler phases, per-chain progress, variable-wise worst R-hat and ESS, and the controller's checks and verdict. Install `[notebook]` for notebook rendering. Notebook stop messages use the widget comm channel and a shared `RunControl`; frontend responsiveness depends on the host notebook's comm scheduling. For independent cancellation during a blocking cell, use the localhost dashboard or `start()`.

## Authenticated localhost

```python
handle = monitor.start(model=model, dashboard=True, progress=False)
print(handle.dashboard_url)
try:
    idata = handle.wait()
    # The dashboard remains readable until close().
finally:
    handle.close()
```

Install the `dashboard` extra first. `Dashboard(*, port=0, title="pymc-monitor", idle_timeout=300)` binds a preallocated socket on `127.0.0.1`. A per-instance token in the navigation path grants an HttpOnly SameSite cookie; treat the URL as a credential. Non-browser API clients can send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Never put a token in query strings or expose this port publicly.

Every route, including assets, requires authentication and validates Host and Origin. Stop is POST-only; unknown runs return 404, and finished or already-stopping runs return 409. The service does not enable cross-origin requests. Static assets are bundled, with a restrictive Content Security Policy and no third-party scripts or analytics. All run-supplied names, errors and hints render as text, not executable HTML. Trace previews show at most 20 elements and 500 points per chain. They are diagnostic previews, not a replacement for posterior plots.

The server is local to the Python host. A notebook running remotely does not make that machine's loopback URL accessible on your laptop. Do not expose the server publicly or publish its token. Remote transport belongs in a separate application.

## Reusable presentation

A shared `Dashboard()` can serve several `start(..., dashboard=dashboard)` handles; each has an isolated run URL and stop control. Removing one handle retains the others, and the idle server shuts down after `idle_timeout` seconds with no runs. Close the shared instance explicitly when done.

`DashboardState(completion_phase="sampling")` is a lock-protected, transport-independent event reducer with `update(event)`, `show_phase`, `show_sampling`, `show_convergence`, `request_stop`, `finish(status)`, and `snapshot()`. Use `completion_phase="downloading"` to keep a cloud dashboard open after sampling ends. Snapshots are independent JSON-safe copies. `render_dashboard_html(*, progress_url, stop_url, token, title)` safely embeds a transport-specific configuration, and `dashboard_assets()` returns bundled HTML, CSS and JavaScript bytes. `static/renderer.js` exports `render(state, root)` for consumers of the same schema; it has no sampler or HTTP dependencies.

A consuming application owns authentication and transport. It can dispatch typed events to the reducer and serve these assets without importing any cloud dependency into pymc-monitor. The local HTTP service is only one adapter for that state.
